content:
Maria: Starting a staged rollout for v4.3.0 to eu-west during the 02:00 UTC change window. Canary at 02:05 (10%). We care about p95, 5xx, embedding cosine drift on the eval set, and synthetic heartbeats. Release notes: https://releases.redwood.ai/4.3.0 :rocket:

Jamal: noted. I've created traffic tag `v4-3-0-canary` and pinned fallback `v4-2-1` in case we need immediate revert. Routing policy set to prefer healthy AZs.

deploy-bot: canary_start by @Maria at 02:05 UTC. canary_id=canary-2026-11-03-01. 10% -> v4-3-0-canary. Monitoring and eval hooks ACTIVE.

eval-bot: EVAL: embedding-regression job started at 02:10 UTC for canary_id=canary-2026-11-03-01. Running 1k eval pairs (semantic-similarity set).

slo-bot: ALERT: embedding-drift-eu-west crossing threshold. avg cosine delta +0.12 vs baseline at 02:12 UTC. threshold=+0.08.

Olivia: Acknowledged. Pulling the eval diffs now. If this is a model-quality regression (not infra noise) we'll hold the ramp and notify product.

Sree: Doing quick smoke and sanity checks. Running scripted queries against the canary endpoints.

Jamal: Traces show no 5xx or p95 issues. KV cache hit ratio normal. Looks like a semantic shift in outputs rather than latency or errors.

Maria: okay hold the ramp to 30%. We have a quality gate: if embedding drift > 0.1 we stop and either pin or rollback. Jamal, lock the legacy pin active.

Jamal: Pin activated: traffic fallback pinned to `v4-2-1`. Customers flagged for early access will remain on previous model by pin.

deploy-bot: ramp paused at 10% per manual hold from @Maria.

eval-bot: EVAL COMPLETE: cosine delta = +0.13 (worse). Top failing pairs attached to the job: ID 1287, 3456, 9992 show notable meaning shifts. Job link: https://ci.redwood.ai/evals/42342

Olivia: I'm attaching a quick diff of embeddings for sample IDs 1287/3456. Differences look consistent across prompts with concept 'pricing' showing drift toward different tokens. Could be tokenization change or a tokenizer mismatch in preprocessing.

Sree: Running a canary request with `--raw-tokenizer` enabled to compare. Command:
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELEASE_KEY" -d '{"input":"price estimate for enterprise"}' 
  https://eu1.api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings?model=v4-3-0-canary | jq .embedding[:8]
```

Jamal: Good call. I see tokenizer differences between v4-2-1 and v4-3-0 where a new tokenizer patch was included in the build. That explains consistent embedding shifts.

Maria: Decision: this is a model-quality regression due to unintended tokenizer bump. Do not rollback infra. We'll pin traffic for mapping-sensitive routes to v4-2-1 and continue investigating. Create a short customer comms note and schedule a hotfix build removing the tokenizer bump.

Jamal: Applied route-level pin for `embeddings:*` routes to `v4-2-1`. Command executed: POST /v1/routing/pins {"routes":["embeddings:*"], "pin_to":"v4-2-1", "scope":"eu-west"}

Olivia: I've updated the deploy docs and observability board to call out the pin and that the SLOs (latency/5xx) are green but quality gate failed. Marking the deployment `partial-pin: embeddings` on the release page.

deploy-bot: canary paused at 10% (quality gate fail). canary_id=canary-2026-11-03-01. Pins applied.

Sree: smoke for non-embedding routes looks fine. Text generation and chat paths are operating within normal limits.

Maria: Excellent triage. Jamal please open a hotfix PR removing tokenizer change and run a new canary once CI passes. Tag the PR with `urgent:embedding-regression`.

Jamal: PR opened: https://git.redwood.ai/r/3456. CI queued. I'll keep the pin until hotfix canary proves stable.

eval-bot: NOTE: Scheduled SLO snapshot at 03:00 UTC will include this window. Alert suppression requested for embedding-drift signals that are now covered by the pin.

Olivia: Filing a short post-release summary in 30m into the release notes with links to eval job and PR.

Maria: Thanks team. If anyone sees customer reports escalate, notify support and copy #customer-success. We'll do a quick sync at 03:15 UTC to decide next steps (hotfix canary or full rollback).
